title: Post-war Nazi network Die Spinne in the Arab world

tellings.quote: into it in the book. I build off of research by Joseph Farrell to suggest that there was an international post-war Nazi network some people call Dishpena the spider

plain: After the Second World War, the claim goes, an international Nazi network known as Die Spinne, German for "the spider", carried on in the Arab world. The philosopher Jason Jorjani tells Michels he goes into it in his book Closer Encounters, building on the research of an author named Joseph Farrell, though he names no particular source for the claim itself. If true, it would mean that organised Nazi circles outlived the war and kept working abroad.
